# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 52 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 52 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_052_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 3 — Trees in Winter

**52:1** He showed me many trees without leaves, which appeared to me to be dry; for they all looked alike. And he said to me: "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, lord," I replied; "they all look alike and are dry." He answered and said to me: "These trees that you see are those who dwell in this present age."

**52:2** "Why then, lord," I asked, "do they appear dry and all alike?" "Because," he said, "neither the righteous nor sinners are distinguishable in this present age, but they resemble one another. For this present age is winter for the righteous who dwell in it, and they are not distinguishable among the sinners.

**52:3** For just as in winter the trees, having shed their leaves, all look alike, and it is not apparent which are withered and which are alive — so too in this present age neither the righteous nor the sinners are apparent, but all appear alike to one another."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the winter/summer allegory of Similitude 3.*
